checks.finding: AC-038 (requirements.md:884) and its mirror TEST-038 (acceptance-tests.md:84) assert that a Block reached after in-memory staging 'confirms no earlier-staged artifact ever reached a live path', naming 'lite-check-source-undefined, output-schema-validation-failed, or snapshot-generation-mismatch' as its fixtures. The subject 'earlier-staged artifact' is unscoped, and the row's own closing clause ('additive to, and structurally subsumes, AC-011's own narrower "no partial artifact" statement') asserts a scope strictly broader than AC-011's enumerated three publication artifacts, which on its face admits Resolver Evidence. REQ-001 step (j) (requirements.md:305-306) stages Resolver Evidence, and step (k) (requirements.md:308-310) schema-validates 'every staged artifact', so for two of AC-038's three named fixtures Evidence is staged EARLIER than the Block: output-schema-validation-failed fires at step (k) and snapshot-generation-mismatch at step (l). For both of those, sibling rows require Evidence to reach its live path: AC-040 (requirements.md:886, scoped 2026-08-27) states 'resolver-evidence.yaml itself IS written recording this diagnostic'; AC-055(b) (requirements.md:901) states 'Resolver Evidence is still written recording this diagnostic'; AC-012 (requirements.md:858) excepts only disabled-legacy-invocation and the self-referential B3 case. DOWNSTREAM FAILURE MODE: the future fixture author for TEST-038's snapshot-generation-mismatch case cannot decide whether to assert resolver-evidence.yaml absent (AC-038's literal text) or present (AC-040/TEST-040, AC-012/TEST-012) - the two assertions cannot both be written into one fixture, and the package's own record (investigation.md:1353-1359) shows a cross-model panel already collided on exactly this write/do-not-write question for a different Block. Only a strained reading rescues AC-038 (that the staged Evidence instance is discarded and a distinct Block record is written instead); neither frozen document states that distinction, and REQ-004's diagnostics[] mandate (requirements.md:526-530) points the other way, since the Block diagnostic is a field OF the staged Evidence. WHY SPEC REVIEW: both rows are frozen Phase-1 acceptance criteria whose scope disagreement exists before any design or task decomposition. WHY MAJOR NOT CRITICAL: the same-diagnostic siblings AC-040/AC-055/AC-012 state the affirmative explicitly, so a careful reader can reconcile; the defect is an unscoped negative that will cause a downstream fixture mismatch rather than an unsatisfiable pair. The remediation sweep recorded at investigation.md:1710-1727 scoped seven sites of exactly this negative-claim class and did not reach this sibling.

AC-049 (requirements.md:895) and TEST-049 (acceptance-tests.md:95) require the post-publication-generation-mismatch fixture to assert '(b) every one of those renames is rolled back to its own PRE-transaction state via the journal before this invocation exits'. The antecedent 'those renames' is clause (a)'s 'every rename in the transaction', and REQ-001 step (m) (requirements.md:317-320) fixes that transaction's target set as '{facet-manifest.yaml, generated/project-context.resolved.json, resolver-evidence.yaml} on full, {capability-summary.yaml, resolver-evidence.yaml} on lite', with REQ-004 (requirements.md:588-594) confirming Evidence 'travels through the identical staged-generation/journaled-transactional-publication mechanism' when published alongside a track's output set. So 'every one of those renames' necessarily includes resolver-evidence.yaml, and rolling it back to its PRE-transaction state before exit means the live path is absent or carries its pre-invocation bytes at exit. Three frozen statements require the opposite terminal state for this same id: (1) Security Boundaries (requirements.md:1240-1251) states every live path is left 'fully absent, fully unchanged ... or - Resolver Evidence only, on any Block except the two REQ-002 names - fully written, at whichever step that Block is reached, the step-(m) Blocks artifact-publication-failed and post-publication-generation-mismatch included', a clause the document records as 'widened 2026-08-27' precisely to cover these two step-(m) Blocks; (2) AC-012 (requirements.md:858) and TEST-012 (acceptance-tests.md:61) require a full Evidence record for every TEST-010 Block fixture except disabled-legacy-invocation and the self-referential B3 case, and TEST-010 (acceptance-tests.md:59) enumerates post-publication-generation-mismatch among its sixteen; (3) REQ-001 step (m) (requirements.md:333-338) states that on any Block reached at (m) 'the invocation writes only Resolver Evidence's own record of that Block ... published directly, not through the journaled transaction'. DOWNSTREAM FAILURE MODE: the TEST-049 fixture and the TEST-012 fixture for the identical diagnostic assert mutually exclusive final states of resolver-evidence.yaml; a Phase-2 implementer choosing to satisfy AC-049 as written destroys the only audit record that a publication briefly succeeded and was rolled back, which is the precise fail-closed evidence obligation REQ-002 and REQ-004 exist to guarantee. WHY SPEC REVIEW: both statements are in the frozen Phase-1 pair and neither can be resolved by design, task, or gate work. WHY CRITICAL: this is a direct workflow-boundary contradiction about an irreversible-publication rollback, and the package itself already declares this exact shape a contradiction - the sibling row AC-047/TEST-047 (requirements.md:893, acceptance-tests.md:93) received per-target scoping in the same ruling-D(2) sweep and records verbatim that 'Asserting only the first half would contradict AC-012; asserting only the second would lose the no-partial-rollback guarantee, so both are required of this one fixture.' AC-049/TEST-049 assert only that first half, for a diagnostic that is likewise not among AC-012's two named exceptions. The remediation record (investigation.md:1710-1727) lists seven scoped sites and does not include this one; the correct form needs no new decision, only the AC-047 per-target shape applied here.

Material negative, empty, boundary, and failure paths implied by the requirements each carry an independently-triggerable acceptance test. All sixteen REQ-002 diagnostic ids have one fixture each plus a clean negative-control fixture (AC-010/TEST-010, acceptance-tests.md:59). Empty states: zero affected components is covered as a legitimate non-Block empty resolution with its own trigger_evaluations[] == [] fixture (requirements.md:1079-1098, AC-018/TEST-018, acceptance-tests.md:67), and Registry Capabilities with conditional_facets: [] are covered (requirements.md:1133-1136). Boundary/failure paths: crash between two renames and an unconvergeable journal (AC-047/TEST-047), pre-publication TOCTOU on digests and on the affected_components set difference alone (AC-040/AC-048, TEST-040/TEST-048), the post-recheck race (AC-049/TEST-049), in-process write/rename failure with journal rollback (AC-039/TEST-039), both sub-cases of output-schema-validation-failed (AC-055/TEST-055), warn/block cardinality including the evaluation-abort exception (AC-056/TEST-056), the two amended sub-triggers from rulings C(1)/C(2) (AC-057/AC-058, TEST-057/TEST-058), provenance-binding negatives for validate-resolver-evidence (AC-050/AC-051), same-facet-name aggregation across and within Capabilities (AC-043/AC-052), and metamorphic completeness including all four two-component truth combinations and input-order permutation (AC-045/TEST-045). The one acknowledged fixture gap - the required-present-empty Lite state - is documented with a citable structural reason (Epic A2's lite_policy schema is additionalProperties: false and admits no required_lite_checks key, so a fixture would not itself pass validate-capability-registry) at acceptance-tests.md:58, and its three sibling states are fixtured, so this is a disclosed limitation rather than uncovered behavior. The Evidence-write obligation for post-publication-generation-mismatch is itself covered, by TEST-012's blanket rule over every TEST-010 fixture; the defect there is that TEST-049 asserts against it, which is reported under CONTRADICTION rather than double-counted here.

Every assumption is either resolved by the investigation record or is an explicitly-owned, explicitly-deferred decision with a named re-verification obligation. The three Assumptions (requirements.md:1288-1311) are: sibling A1/A2/A3 contracts landing unmodified (each confirmed Spec-Review-Status: Passed at investigation.md INV-002, with a stated follow-up-edit obligation if any changes materially); the protected-suffix reservation for resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1} being live in guard-invariants.json (INV-003, with an explicit 'if it is not yet live, re-verify then and choose unprotected-first-then-register instead' branch); and the SKILL.md unprotected status (INV-017, explicitly labelled a live-repository snapshot to be re-verified at implementation-task start, not a permanent guarantee). Open Questions (requirements.md:1315-1333) are each disposed of rather than left dangling: OQ-001 and OQ-002 are declared out of this feature's scope with a named future owner (a future caller's contract; a future epic invoking compare-facet-manifest-staleness) and are consistent with the matching Non-goals at requirements.md:794-796; OQ-003 is stated as resolved by INV-020 with a concrete file:line anchor plus a position-sensitive fingerprint (AC-053/TEST-053). The one cross-epic gap that is genuinely unresolved - Epic A2's Registry schema carrying no required_lite_checks source (INV-019) - is named as an explicit, owned prerequisite with owner, scope, and migration stated (requirements.md:140-163), narrowed to the required-enforcement Lite path only, is disclaimed as out of this feature's authority in Non-goals (requirements.md:782-786), and is carried into a Risk with the reason it is surfaced now rather than papered over (requirements.md:1337-1367). No assumption is left as an unowned 'to be decided at implementation time' item.

Every human-approval, governance, and irreversible-change boundary the requirements imply is named and testable. Human-application boundary: the Resolver script family's code content is staged under specs/<feature>/human-copy/ for human application via apply-human-copy because the target path is protected (requirements.md:965-975), scoped explicitly to the three scripts' immutable code and explicitly NOT the mechanism by which generated artifacts acquire content; the test.yml registration likewise resolves through a human cp action with a MANIFEST.sha256 entry (AC-026/TEST-026, acceptance-tests.md:75). Scope boundary against protected/plugin surface: Non-goals forbid editing plugins/** and every A1-A4 contract file (requirements.md:775-781, 805-810), and AC-032/TEST-032 (acceptance-tests.md:81) lock it with a git diff over this package's own two registration commits, with the manual review record at acceptance-tests.md:130-133. Approval-sidecar boundary: the Resolver never writes any *.approval.json sidecar, sdd/.approved-context/ anchor, or guard-invariants.json (requirements.md:1211-1216). Irreversible-change boundary: the publication transaction's Prepare/Journal/Commit/Post-publication-verification/Complete sequence, its journal-based (never bare-unlink) rollback, and the mandatory crash-recovery scan are each fixed normatively (requirements.md:317-338, 385-386, 1261-1268) and are each locked by fixtures (AC-039/AC-047/AC-049/AC-054). Governance of the amendments themselves: investigation.md's '## Amendment Re-Review Context' (investigation.md:792 ff.) meets the calibration's four-element evidence bar - full un-abbreviated commit hashes (investigation.md:800-812, 1266, 1452-1464, 1710-1711), per-document SHA-256 at each amendment commit (investigation.md:813-834, 1286, 1466-1475, 1736-1742), verbatim dated human approval quotations for rulings A/B (2026-08-24), C (2026-08-26) and D(1)/D(2) (2026-08-27, including the withdrawn half quoted verbatim at investigation.md:1364 and 1411), and commit/SHA-256 citations for every referenced later-phase artifact (investigation.md:864-887) - so the phase-sequencing suppression applies and no finding here rests on the mere presence of later-phase references. The internal inconsistency in AC-049's rollback assertion is reported under CONTRADICTION and is not double-counted as a missing boundary, since the boundary itself is stated and has an owning fixture.

The specification fixes product behavior at a level that does not require an implementation-policy reviewer to invent it. The CLI surface is fully fixed with flag-by-flag required/default semantics and the rationale for --feature never being inferred (requirements.md:231-248); the processing order is a fully enumerated step sequence (0)/(a)-(m) with the staging-then-publish invariant stated structurally rather than as a per-step promise (requirements.md:250-355); the Block taxonomy is a closed sixteen-row machine-readable table with a trigger condition per row (requirements.md:369-386); the exit-code contract is fixed per value (AC-013/TEST-013); the new artifact's schema is field-by-field specified including cardinality, exact-set, bidirectional-consistency, and stable-sort rules (requirements.md:474-621); the caller-side integration contract names a concrete file:line insertion anchor with a position-sensitive fingerprint rather than a heading-text guess (requirements.md:733-740, AC-053); track-exclusive output sets, byte-identity scope and its one named divergence, and the multi-component union-match and facet-name aggregation rules are each stated with their rationale (requirements.md:415-472, 1113-1132). Terms that could otherwise drift are pinned in Field Definitions (requirements.md:906-961), including an explicit statement that the removed 'representative branch' concept is depended on nowhere. Every REQ maps to at least one AC, and every AC except the three documented Global rows maps 1:1 to a TEST row, with the counts reconciled and the exception class documented in the acceptance-tests preamble (acceptance-tests.md:8-46). The two findings above are corrections to existing rows whose intended behavior is already stated normatively elsewhere in the same documents (REQ-001 step (m), REQ-002's two-exception rule, REQ-004, Security Boundaries), so the design reviewer inherits a scoping defect to be fixed, not missing product behavior to be invented.
